Stepwise forward regression

Source: R/blr-stepwise-forward-regression.R
blr_step_p_forward.Rd

Build regression model from a set of candidate predictor variables by entering predictors based on p values, in a stepwise manner until there is no variable left to enter any more.

Usage

blr_step_p_forward(model, ...)

# Default S3 method
blr_step_p_forward(model, penter = 0.3, details = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'blr_step_p_forward'
plot(x, model = NA, print_plot = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

model

An object of class glm; the model should include all candidate predictor variables. Only binary logistic regression models (binomial family with logit link) are supported. Weighted models (any prior weight other than 1) and grouped binomial models (cbind(successes, failures) or proportions) are not supported; the model must be fitted with model = TRUE, y = TRUE.

...

Other arguments.

penter

p value; variables with p value less than penter will enter into the model

details

Logical; if TRUE, will print the regression result at each step.

x

An object of class blr_step_p_forward.

print_plot

logical; if TRUE, prints the plot else returns a plot object.

Value

blr_step_p_forward returns an object of class "blr_step_p_forward". An object of class "blr_step_p_forward" is a list containing the following components:

model

model with the least AIC; an object of class glm Only binary logistic regression models (binomial family with logit link) are supported. Weighted models (any prior weight other than 1) and grouped binomial models (cbind(successes, failures) or proportions) are not supported; the model must be fitted with model = TRUE, y = TRUE.

steps

number of steps

predictors

variables added to the model

aic

akaike information criteria

bic

bayesian information criteria

dev

deviance

indvar

predictors

References

Chatterjee, Samprit and Hadi, Ali. Regression Analysis by Example. 5th ed. N.p.: John Wiley & Sons, 2012. Print.

Kutner, MH, Nachtsheim CJ, Neter J and Li W., 2004, Applied Linear Statistical Models (5th edition). Chicago, IL., McGraw Hill/Irwin.

Aliased terms

A model with aliased (perfectly collinear) coefficients is rejected with an error, because the Wald test used to enter or remove terms does not exist for them. Remove the aliased terms and refit.

See also

Other variable selection procedures: blr_step_aic_backward(), blr_step_aic_both(), blr_step_aic_forward(), blr_step_p_backward()

Examples

# stepwise forward regression
model <- glm(honcomp ~ female + read + science, data = hsb2,
  family = binomial(link = 'logit'))
blr_step_p_forward(model)
#> Forward Selection Method    
#> ---------------------------
#> 
#> Candidate Terms: 
#> 
#> 1. female 
#> 2. read 
#> 3. science 
#> 
#> We are selecting variables based on p value...
#> 
#> Variables Entered: 
#> 
#> - read 
#> - female 
#> - science 
#> 
#> 
#> Final Model Output 
#> ------------------
#> 
#>                              Model Overview                              
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> Data Set    Resp Var    Obs.    Df. Model    Df. Residual    Convergence 
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------
#>   hsb2      honcomp     200         3            196            TRUE     
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>                     Response Summary                     
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#> Outcome        Frequency        Outcome        Frequency 
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#>    0              147              1              53     
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>                   Maximum Likelihood Estimates                    
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#>  Parameter     DF    Estimate    Std. Error    z value    Pr(>|z|) 
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#> (Intercept)    1     -12.7772       1.9755    -6.4677      0.0000 
#>    read        1      0.1035        0.0258     4.0186       1e-04 
#>   female1      1      1.4825        0.4474     3.3139       9e-04 
#>   science      1      0.0948        0.0305     3.1129      0.0019 
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>  Association of Predicted Probabilities and Observed Responses  
#> ---------------------------------------------------------------
#> % Concordant          0.8561          Somers' D        0.7136   
#> % Discordant          0.1425          Gamma            0.7147   
#> % Tied                0.0014          Tau-a            0.2794   
#> Pairs                  7791           c                0.8568   
#> ---------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#> 
#>                  Selection Summary                   
#> ----------------------------------------------------
#>         Variable                                        
#> Step    Entered       AIC         BIC       Deviance    
#> ----------------------------------------------------
#>    1    read        183.0630    189.6596    179.0630    
#>    2    female      176.8874    186.7824    170.8874    
#>    3    science     168.2364    181.4296    160.2364    
#> ----------------------------------------------------

# stepwise forward regression plot
model <- glm(honcomp ~ female + read + science, data = hsb2,
  family = binomial(link = 'logit'))
k <- blr_step_p_forward(model)
#> Forward Selection Method    
#> ---------------------------
#> 
#> Candidate Terms: 
#> 
#> 1. female 
#> 2. read 
#> 3. science 
#> 
#> We are selecting variables based on p value...

#> 
#> - read 
#> - female 
#> - science 
#> 
#> 
#> Final Model Output 
#> ------------------
#> 
#>                              Model Overview                              
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> Data Set    Resp Var    Obs.    Df. Model    Df. Residual    Convergence 
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------
#>   hsb2      honcomp     200         3            196            TRUE     
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>                     Response Summary                     
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#> Outcome        Frequency        Outcome        Frequency 
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#>    0              147              1              53     
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>                   Maximum Likelihood Estimates                    
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#>  Parameter     DF    Estimate    Std. Error    z value    Pr(>|z|) 
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#> (Intercept)    1     -12.7772       1.9755    -6.4677      0.0000 
#>    read        1      0.1035        0.0258     4.0186       1e-04 
#>   female1      1      1.4825        0.4474     3.3139       9e-04 
#>   science      1      0.0948        0.0305     3.1129      0.0019 
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>  Association of Predicted Probabilities and Observed Responses

#> % Concordant          0.8561          Somers' D        0.7136

plot(k)

# final model
k$model
